title: Does the model remember the start?
hook: You told it your cat's name twenty words ago. Can it still see it?

knows: that a language model predicts the next token from the text before it
doesNotKnow: that it can only use a fixed amount of recent text (its context window)

misconception: The model remembers everything in the conversation.
objective: The learner can explain that a model answers only from the tokens inside its window, so anything earlier is not remembered less but is not there at all.

claims.text: With a 20-token document and a window of the last 8 tokens, positions 13-20 are visible, so a fact at a random position is usable with chance 8/20 = 40%; a fact at position 5 is outside. The stage shows the window share as "8 of 20 = 40%".
claims.source: share(w) = w / 20 and visible() in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: Dropping a fact at 20 random positions counts how many land inside the current window (mulberry32 seeds 1, 2, 3, ... in order, untuned; seed 1 at window 8 gives 7 of 20). The long-run share inside an 8-token window is 8/20 = 40%.
claims.source: spread(8, 500) in Demo.tsx, mulberry32 seeds 1-500, untuned. The stage's 'Drop at 20 random spots' uses seeds 1, 2, 3, ... in order (untuned; seed 1 gives 7 of 20). · Fact-check 2026-10-13: Mean over seeds 1-500 is 7.94. · Fact-check 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Demo.tsx has no spread(); re-ran hits(seed, 8) from the Demo.tsx model: seed 1 = 7 of 20; mean over seeds 1-500 = 7.938 (39.7%); seeds 1-20000 = 40.1%.

claims.text: The 20-token document and window sizes are invented for the toy; real models have windows of thousands of tokens or more.
claims.source: Brief 26 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md. Window sizes vary by model and are given in each model's documentation.

claims.text: Real language models answer from a fixed-length context of tokens; text outside it is not available to the model for that answer.
claims.source: About real systems: Vaswani et al. 2017, 'Attention is all you need' (NeurIPS; attention over a fixed-length input sequence); Brown et al. 2020, 'Language models are few-shot learners' (GPT-3, context window of 2,048 tokens).

recall.question: In a very long chat, a model forgets an instruction you gave at the very start. What is the most likely reason?
options: The instruction fell outside the model's context window
The model decided the instruction was unimportant
The model's memory of it faded gradually
recall.why: A model only uses the tokens in its window. Once the start of the chat scrolls out, the instruction is not faded; for that answer it is simply absent.
